## papers 3.0.0b7

- **Fetching the free PDF of an entry.** `papers file fetch KEY...`
  downloads a PDF of the entry and attaches it as `papers file attach`
  does; `--missing` does it for the entries that have no PDF;
  `papers add --doi DOI --fetch-pdf` and `papers fetch --pdf DOI` (no
  library) too. papers tries the publisher's page, the open-access copies
  that OpenAlex lists (repositories included) and arXiv, the published
  version first, and says which version it attached and from where. Many
  publishers refuse programs (Wiley, PNAS, Science, Elsevier among them):
  then papers attaches nothing and prints the links to open in a browser.
  A broken link is first repaired from the files already on the computer,
  nothing is downloaded or attached twice, and `papers file fetch
  --upgrade` replaces a preprint or accepted manuscript by the published
  version when it can be downloaded. The version of each fetched PDF is
  kept in `.papers/files.json`; `papers list --pdf-version accepted` lists
  those entries. The OpenAlex key and an email address can be given in the
  environment (`OPENALEX_API_KEY`, `PAPERS_MAILTO`).
- **`papers file fix` finds the file of a broken link in more places**: by
  checksum in the library itself (a file renamed by hand), in the pool,
  and in the other libraries of the computer that papers has a history of.
- **`--openalex`**, next to `--scholar`: a full-text search of a PDF's
  metadata on OpenAlex, an open catalogue (by alex-robinson).
- **Duplicates and file names**: the LaTeX decoder of the same-paper rule
  reads the text as LaTeX does (`T\^ete` gave `Tet̂e`), and the ASCII
  transliteration is now AnyAscii (permissive license, all scripts):
  Chinese gives `beijing` in a file name (was `bei-jing`). `papers list
  WORDS` ignores accents and LaTeX (`Muller` finds `M{\"u}ller`).
- **Faster**: `papers status` no longer reads every linked PDF (2.8 s to
  0.3 s on a library of 356 entries), `pull` of 10 000 entries 17 s to
  3.5 s, the history's pruning and undo, and the start of every command.
- **The history**: a damaged file of the history (after a power cut) stops
  undo with a clear message instead of a traceback, and changes nothing.
- **The specification** in `design/` no longer depends on Python: its
  data tables are in `design/data/`, its tests are listed in
  `design/tests.md`, and `design/cases/` holds conformance cases that any
  implementation can run (by alex-robinson, who is writing a Rust version
  for Papers Desktop).
- Many fixes found while writing that Rust version: exit codes, `--porcelain`
  lines, `--dry-run` that moved files, crashes on network answers, and more
  (#188 to #219).
